text:
rachel: Heads up — Nebula Freight (acct NF-501) has an outstanding INV-009210 for $29,760. Client emailed asking to pause action and proposed paying 25% now, rest over 3 months. Card on file declined on retry.

collections-bot: Dunning email #4 sent to ap@nebulafreight.com. Last CC auth: decline code 14. Collections referral threshold: balances >$25k and >45 days.

omar: Invoice split below: subscription $9,600; usage/overage $20,200; credits $40. Usage spike traced to webhook loop 2026-01-12. Client claims partner integration caused it.

ben: For this size, we usually require 30% upfront or ACH/wire. Also need signed settlement addendum for multi-month plans. Any legal pushback?

maya: Legal: settlement addendum required for anything longer than 60 days. No permanent write-offs without VP Finance sign-off. We can draft a short-form addendum.

rachel: My read: offer 30% now + 3 monthly installments OR accept their 25% now if they agree to immediate ACH and include their partner logs within 7 days for audit. Also require no-chargeback clause.

omar: Ops: If partner logs show misconfig, consider a one-time 15% credit on the overage only, not the subscription. That would reduce amount slightly and make plan more palatable.

ben: Collections perspective: if they stall, recovery usually 40-60% after referral but takes ~6 months. Given historic relationship (they're a long-time customer), leaning to negotiated plan with addendum.

rachel: I'll send client two options and attach draft addendum. If they pick 25% ask, escalate to Jules (VP Finance) for sign-off.

nebulafreight-ap (external): CFO on travel, can confirm 25% by EOD tomorrow and provide partner logs within 5 business days. Asking for waiver of late fees.

rachel: We'll waive late fees if they provide logs within 5 days and pay 25% via wire by tomorrow EOD, but VP Finance must sign off on the credit/plan. Sending payment instructions now.
